name: Reconstructed store-residence on Lake Street, as Gifford draws it

documented_range.note: Drawn standing beside the first Tremont House (1833-1839) in Gifford's retrospective view of its street; taken as standing on 1 July 1835 on the owner's reading of the drawing (T-3605). No dated record of this building is known.

position.symbolic_location: Lake Street, lake north clark to dearborn: drawn store K of Gifford's row
position.note: Placed in the drawn order along the face, at stations 75.21-81.01 m of the face line (The block's Lake Street face, from the Clark corner east; the row stands on the line the Tremont House's own Lake Street gable stands on, 2.52 m inside the platted face, so the plank walk passes in front of every door.), with 0.89 m between neighbours. Drawn at x 712-776 px of the 1637 px plate. The face is the drawing's (read through the Tremont's solved camera, data/reconstruction/1835_gifford_street_faces.json camera); the station is fitted, not measured.

derivation.reason: The drawing has no scale; the rows are fitted to the platted face.

footprint.note: 5.80 m of frontage proportioned from the drawn bays and 10.00 m deep inside the C2 typology band; neither is a measurement.

stories.note: READ OFF GIFFORD'S DRAWING of the first Tremont House and its street (gifford_tremont_house_no_1): a story-and-a-half store, gable to the street, door between two windows; board lettered BOOTS & SHOES. Inferred, because it is a picture of this building; the drawing is retrospective, and taking it as the street on 1 July 1835 is the owner's reading of 2026-11-15 (T-3605, docs/LIBERTIES.md L-gifford-street-faces-3605).

occupants.note: SEATED BY THE STREET-FACE ADOPTION POLICY (docs/STREET-FACE-ADOPTION.md, the owner's ruling of 2026-08-29 for T-0354, extended 2026-08-30 for T-0416; liberty L212). The newspaper register places this business on Dearborn Street AND NOTHING NARROWER — 2 printings, 1834-06-04 to 1834-07-09, claims chicago_democrat_1834_06_04#c024, chicago_democrat_1834_07_09#c027 — so it takes the STREET FACE and not a lot. THE ROOF ENDS ITS PLATTED TIER AGAINST Dearborn Street, so it is a corner building and stands on that street as well as on the one its lot faces — the owner's ruling of 2026-08-30 (T-0416). Nothing about the roof changed and no geometry was raised to seat this business. WHICH roof on that face it is given is an allocation by tools/adopt_street_faces.py and not a reading of any source, and nothing here says this business stood nearer the corner than any other on the same face. THE ROOF'S OWN EXISTENCE, POSITION AND FOOTPRINT REMAIN CONJECTURAL and are unchanged by the adoption: the business is documented, the building under it is not, and this attribute is graded `reconstructed` because the invented part is the whole of the placement.

research_note: RECONSTRUCTED FROM A PICTURE. Gifford draws this store in the row beside the first Tremont House; the owner ruled on 2026-11-15 that the drawing is a reasonable view of 1835 and the street is to be built to it. The drawn form is inferred from the drawing; the building's presence in July 1835, its exact frontage and its station are reconstructed. Its occupants, if any, are dealt by the town's housing tools and graded by their own records.
